Scholarships of Distinction

Request Info

UNA's Scholarships of Distinction

The University of North Alabama's Scholarships of Distinction is designed for outstanding students interested in fields of Accounting, Computing, Data Analytics, and Engineering.

These programs provide generous scholarships and excellent learning experiences for motivated students. Students majoring in Accounting, Computer Science, Computer Information Systems, Data Analytics, Engineering, and Industrial Professions are eligible to apply. 

Scholarships of Distinction

Accounting

UNA offers a Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting, a Master of Accountancy (MAcc), and a Master of Business Administration (MBA) in Accounting. North Alabama emphasizes teaching excellence in our accounting programs through innovation, applied research, engagement of faculty and students with the business community, and the use of technology to enhance the quality of our programs. 

Apply Now

Engineering and Industrial Professions

The Department of Engineering and Industrial Professions is seeking applicants for Scholarships of Distinction in Engineering. UNA offers two undergraduate degree programs: the Bachelor of Engineering (B.Eng.) and the Bachelor of Science in Engineering Technology (B.S.). The Bachelor of Engineering includes concentrations in Chemical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Power Generation Engineering, and Engineering Management, while the Bachelor of Science in Engineering Technology offers options in Electromechanical Engineering Technology and Occupational and Environmental Health and Safety Engineering Technology. These programs combine rigorous academics with hands-on laboratory experiences and industry engagement to prepare graduates for careers in engineering, engineering technology, and related technical professions.

Apply Now

Computing and Data Analytics

UNA’s degree offerings in computing and data analytics integrate applied and hands-on learning to prepare students to enter the workforce with skills that are applicable in a variety of options in their field such as software engineering, web development, information security, data analysis, or database management. Majors included are Computer Information Systems (CIS), Computer Science (CS), Data Analytics, and Information Technology (IT). 

Apply Now

FAQs


Students must be majoring in one of our distinctive scholarship programs. UNA students majoring in Accounting*, Computer Science, Computer Information Systems, Data Analytics, Information Technology, Engineering, or Occupational and Environmental Health and Safety  are eligible to apply. Find your major listed below to view program-specific requirements.

*The graduate accounting programs have separate eligibility requirements from the Bachelor of Business Administration in Accounting. Please see below for more information. 

Undergraduate Student Eligibility by Major: 

Accounting:

  • First-time Freshman: minimum 3.3 high school GPA and 26 ACT preferred
  • Transfer Student: minimum 3.3 undergraduate GPA; junior standing preferred; B or better in AC 291 and AC 292
  • Current UNA Student: minimum 3.3 undergraduate GPA; junior standing preferred; B or better in AC 291 and AC 292

Computer Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Analytics, and Information Technology:

  • First-time Freshman: minimum 3.0 high school GPA OR 24 ACT composite
  • Transfer Student: minimum 3.0 GPA in all post-secondary coursework
  • Current UNA Student: minimum 3.0 GPA overall; minimum 3.0 in-major GPA

Engineering Technology:

The requirement for students in the Department of Engineering and Industrial Professions is a 3.30 GPA*. Students applying for this program scholarship are also required to have a 25+ on ACT Composite, Math, and Science scores.

*This program is targeting first-time and transfer students; however, if funds are available, sophomore Engineering majors may also qualify.

Occupational Health Science:

  • First-time Freshman: minimum 3.0 high school GPA or 25 or higher ACT composite
  • Transfer Student: minimum 3.0 GPA in all post-secondary coursework
  • Current UNA Student: minimum 3.0 GPA overall

Graduate Student Eligibility by Major: 

MAcc and MBA in Accounting:

  • Minimum 3.5 undergraduate GPA
  • Undergraduate degree must have been obtained from UNA

All Scholarship of Distinction applicants must be U.S. Citizens.


  • Accounting, Computing, and Data Analytics: students applying for priority consideration for Fall 2026 must apply by June 1, 2026.
  • Engineering and Industrial Professions: students applying for priority consideration for Fall 2026 must apply by June 1, 2026.

What if I do not live in the dorm?

If you do not live in the dorm, your scholarship will not include room and board. Based on the scholarship level according to your major, you will still receive the tuition and fees. 


Can this scholarship be stacked with the Academic or Presidential Scholarship?

No – Scholarships of Distinction cannot be combined with these scholarships. These scholarships are designed to take the place of standard UNA academic scholarships. Other types of scholarships may be available.


 What qualifications do I have to meet or maintain to keep my scholarship?

Scholarships of Distinction in Accounting:

  • BBA in Accounting: Must maintain an overall 3.3 GPA (no major-specific GPA requirement) and must complete at least 30 credit hours of progress toward their degree per academic year.
  • Master of Accountancy and MBA in Accounting: Must maintain an overall 3.0 GPA.
  • Students falling below any of the above criteria for either accounting degree program will have a one-semester probationary period to get back up to the required standards.
  • If a student changes to a major outside of accounting, the Scholarship of Distinction will be discontinued.

Scholarships of Distinction in Computing & Data Analytics, Engineering, or Occupational and Environmental Health and Safety:

  • Must maintain a 3.0 overall and in-major GPA and must complete at least 24 credit hours of progress toward their degree per academic year.
  • Students falling below any of these criteria will have a one-semester probationary period to get back up to the required standards.
  • If a student changes their major to another Scholarship of Distinction major, they retain their scholarship. If a student changes to a major outside of computing, data analytics, or engineering technology, they lose their scholarship. However, students may still be eligible for other UNA scholarships for which they are qualified.

Follow the detailed instructions below to complete the application process.  We want to know more about you. You should create your video and obtain your recommendation letter before you fill out the scholarship application. Scholarship levels are as follows:

Accounting Scholarship Levels:  

  • Purple - up to $13,000/year 
  • Gold - up to $11,000/year
  • Silver - up to $9,000/year

Note: You must be a Resident of the US to apply. 

*On-campus award levels may include tuition, fees, room, and board. 

*Off-campus award levels may include tuition and fees. 

MAcc and MBA in Accounting Scholarship Levels:  

  • Purple - 50% of tuition and fees
  • Gold - 35% of tuition and fees
  • Silver - 20% of tuition and fees

This application will require a short video and a professional resume.

Scholarship video criteria:

  • The video should be 3-4 minutes in length.
  • Professional video equipment is not necessary to record your video. The video can be recorded with a smartphone, tablet, webcam, etc. The video will be judged on the quality of the content, not the quality of the video production.
  • Save your video using a popular video format (i.e., mov, mp4)

Your video should address the following questions/topics:

  • Explain your background/experience with accountancy/business administration.
  • Share a couple of personal accomplishments that you are most proud of.
  • What are your favorite school subjects? Explain why.
  • What career would you like to pursue? Explain why.

Criteria for the recommendation letter:

  • A one-page letter is adequate.
  • The letter should come from someone that can speak to your academic background and potential. This letter may be from someone such as a high school teacher, high school counselor, college instructor, or academic advisor.
  • The letter should address the applicant’s academic background and potential for completing an accountancy degree at the University of North Alabama.

Once you have applied (and uploaded your resume & video), we will be contact you via email or text about the next steps!

The Department of Engineering and Industrial Professions is seeking applicants for our Scholarship of Distinction in Engineering.

Engineering Scholarship Levels:  

  • Purple - up to $13,000/year 
  • Gold - up to $11,000/year
  • Silver - up to $9,000/year

Note: You must be a Resident of the US to apply. 

*On-campus award levels may include tuition, fees, room, and board. 

*Off-campus award levels may include tuition and fees. 

This application will require a short video and a professional resume.

Here are the criteria for the resume:

  • Limit the length of your resume to one page.
  • Include sections for education, work experience, and extra-curricular activities.
  • This is your opportunity to highlight areas beyond your academic work that can show evidence of work ethic, initiative, engagement with industry/community, etc.

Here are the criteria for the scholarship video:

  • The video should be 2-3 minutes in length.
  • Professional video equipment is not necessary to record your video. The video can be recorded with a smartphone, tablet, etc. The video will be judged on the quality of the content, not the quality of the video production.
  • Upload your video to a video sharing service (YouTube, Vimeo, etc.) and paste a link directly to your video in a Word document or PDF to upload in your application. You cannot upload the video itself directly to the application.
  • You (the applicant) must appear in the video; not necessarily for the full 2-3 minutes (although, that is acceptable), but you must make an appearance.

Your video should address the following questions/topics:

  • Briefly introduce yourself.
  • Share with us why you want to come to UNA.
  • Describe which of the three engineering technology options you plan to pursue and why.
  • Describe an ideal career for you (job title, company, industry, city/state/country, etc.).
  • List and describe the skills (not subjects like "math" and "science") you think are necessary for success as an engineering technology student, and to what degree you possess these skills.

Please email eip@una.edu with any questions or issues.

Once you have applied (and uploaded your resume & video), we will be contact you via email or text about the next steps!
